title: A Solar Blast Missed Earth by Nine Days in 2012

scenes.text: In 2012, a giant solar blast missed Earth by nine days.
On July 23, plasma left the Sun at over two thousand kilometres a second.
It crossed Earth's orbit, but our planet wasn't there. Nine days earlier, it would have been.
Scientists say it would likely have matched the 1859 Carrington storm, the biggest ever recorded.
One insurance study put that damage at up to 2.6 trillion dollars.
Nine days. That's all that saved us.

description:
A solar blast in July 2012 crossed Earth's orbit just nine days after our planet was in its path.
Researchers say it would likely have matched the 1859 Carrington storm, with far worse effects today.
Did you know how close it was?
first_comment: If it had hit, how long do you think the power would have stayed off?
